 How Investors Are Reacting To AT&T (T) Satellite Phone Handoff
 SA Sasha Jovanovic November 10, 2026, 09:19 UTC Share AT&T reported that in October 2026 it completed what it believes is the first successful handoff between a ground cellular network and a direct to device satellite network with AST SpaceMobile, Ericsson and Nokia, aiming to extend coverage to remote US locations using standard smartphones.
 The collaboration highlights how AT&T is working to fuse terrestrial and space based connectivity, which could influence future network investment priorities, operating costs and service reliability in sparsely served areas.
 We will now assess how AT&T’s direct to device satellite handoff milestone could reshape the existing investment narrative around its network strategy.
 Scan beyond AT&T and spot other connectivity plays that are pushing into harder to reach coverage areas with a curated short list of 42 power grid technology and infrastructure stocks .
 Advertisement AT&T Investment Narrative Recap
 To stay on board as a shareholder in AT&T, you need to believe that heavy spending on 5G, fiber and network convergence can translate into steadier recurring service revenue and higher earnings over time. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St leans on that thesis, while still flagging execution on copper retirement and cost take out as a key test.
 In the short term, the direct to device satellite handoff and broader rural coverage push may not move the main needle. The primary focus is still network economics and free cash flow. The larger near term swing factor remains whether AT&T can take out roughly US$6b of legacy copper costs while keeping device subsidies from eroding margins.
 The satellite handoff milestone aligns with AT&T’s broader push toward network convergence that the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St highlights as a core catalyst. If everyday smartphones can move between fiber backed terrestrial coverage and satellite service without noticeable interruption, that supports the story of more resilient connectivity for high value accounts.
 The expanded collaboration with Smart Meter around Global SIM Advanced is closely related. It shows AT&T trying to turn better reach into stickier enterprise and healthcare relationships, which can be important if consumer equipment promotions weigh on profitability. Execution risk is real, because the operator still carries high debt and lower current profit margins than a year ago.
 AT&T's narrative projects US$135.6b revenue and US$18.8b earnings by 2029. This is based on 1.7% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of about US$5.7b from US$13.1b today.

 One point bearish analysts worry about is whether AT&T can squeeze real earnings from all this convergence work. Before this satellite news, the lowest forecasts were for roughly flat revenue near US$130.2b by 2029 and earnings of about US$18.3b. That is a much more cautious story.
